processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Solution treatment at 1050°C for 2 h followed by water quench to produce fully austenitic matrix.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: Charpy V-notch (CVN) specimen for impact energy; Brinell indentation for hardness

structures.overall_structure: Fully austenitic matrix in the solution-treated (1050°C, 2 h) and water-quenched condition

unmapped_findings: Chemical composition of this sample's heat (Table I, row 3, b0013/figure_unlabelled_001): Si 1.07, C 0.90, Mn 29.11, P 0.070, Mo 0.37, Al 9.25, Cu 0.10 wt.%; S not reported.

Tensile properties for this exact 0.07% P solution-treated sample are not explicitly tabulated; the closest Table II 'No Calcium treatment' solution-treated (2 h) rows are Si 1.0/P 0.06 (YS 458 MPa, UTS 687 MPa, 44% elongation) and Si 1.4/P 0.06 (YS 549 MPa, UTS 766 MPa, 36% elongation).

Dynamic fracture toughness (DFT) is not reported for this 0.07% P solution-treated sample; Table IV DFT values cover 0.59% Si/0.002% P, 1.07% Si/0.001% P, 1.56% Si/0.002% P, and 0.94% Si/0.043% P variants.

Phosphorus-induced short-range ordering (SRO) is suggested as the mechanism lowering the {001} cleavage strength and causing the cleavage-like dendritic fracture observed in the 0.07% P solution-treated sample (b0043).
